techniques.name: Focused Attention
techniques.tagline: Anchor your attention, gently return when it wanders
techniques.why: Sustained-attention practice measurably reduces mind-wandering and strengthens the brain networks involved in attentional control.
techniques.citation: Lutz, Slagter, Dunne & Davidson (2008), Trends in Cognitive Sciences — attentional control mechanisms in focused-attention meditation.

sessions.title: Breath Anchor
sessions.instruction: Rest attention on the breath. Each time the mind wanders, gently escort it back — no judgment, just return.

sessions.title: Steady Attention
sessions.instruction: Rest attention on the breath. Each time the mind wanders, gently escort it back — no judgment, just return.

sessions.title: Deep Focus
sessions.instruction: Rest attention on the breath. Each time the mind wanders, gently escort it back — no judgment, just return.

techniques.name: Body Scan
techniques.tagline: A slow sweep of attention through the body
techniques.why: Body scan practice is well-supported for reducing somatic anxiety and easing sleep onset, and is a core module of clinically validated MBSR programs.
techniques.citation: Kabat-Zinn (1990); meta-analysis in Gotink et al. (2015), PLOS ONE — MBSR/MBCT outcomes across 209 studies.

sessions.title: Quick Body Scan
sessions.instruction: Starting at your feet, slowly move your attention upward through the body. Simply notice each area — no need to change anything.

sessions.title: Full Body Scan
sessions.instruction: Starting at your feet, slowly move your attention upward through the body. Simply notice each area — no need to change anything.

sessions.title: Sleep Body Scan
sessions.instruction: Starting at your feet, slowly move your attention upward through the body, releasing tension as you go. Let this ease you toward sleep.

techniques.name: Loving-Kindness
techniques.tagline: Direct warmth toward yourself and others
techniques.why: Loving-kindness (metta) meditation reliably increases positive emotion and social connection, and has been shown to reduce implicit bias toward others.
techniques.citation: Fredrickson, Cohn, Coffey, Pek & Finkel (2008), Journal of Personality and Social Psychology — broaden-and-build effects of loving-kindness meditation.

sessions.title: Kindness for Yourself
sessions.instruction: Silently offer yourself: 'May I be safe. May I be at ease. May I be well.' Let the phrases settle before repeating.

sessions.title: Kindness for a Loved One
sessions.instruction: Picture someone you care about. Silently offer: 'May you be safe. May you be at ease. May you be well.'

sessions.title: Kindness for a Hard Relationship
sessions.instruction: Bring to mind someone you have friction with. Gently offer the same phrases — you are not condoning, only softening your own heart.

techniques.name: Open Mindfulness
techniques.tagline: Notice thoughts and feelings without judgment
techniques.why: Standard MBSR-style open-awareness practice has strong RCT evidence for reducing anxiety, depression, and chronic pain.
techniques.citation: Goyal et al. (2014), JAMA Internal Medicine — meta-analysis of 47 RCTs on mindfulness meditation programs.

sessions.title: Arriving
sessions.instruction: Let thoughts and feelings arise and pass, like clouds. You don't need to follow them or push them away — just notice.

sessions.title: Open Awareness
sessions.instruction: Let thoughts and feelings arise and pass, like clouds. You don't need to follow them or push them away — just notice.

sessions.title: Deep Stillness
sessions.instruction: Let thoughts and feelings arise and pass, like clouds. You don't need to follow them or push them away — just notice.
